taxonomy.subtopic: Loss of elastic recoil and expiratory flow limitation in emphysema

questions.stem_html: A 66-year-old man with a 45-pack-year smoking history has progressive exertional dyspnea. Pulmonary function testing shows a decreased FEV1/FVC ratio, increased total lung capacity, and decreased diffusing capacity. The accompanying flow-volume loop has a scooped expiratory limb. Which structural change most directly produces the abnormal expiratory contour?

options.text_html: Loss of alveolar elastic recoil and radial traction, causing dynamic collapse of small airways during expiration
Uniform thickening of the alveolar-capillary membrane, increasing airway tethering
Increased surfactant production, raising alveolar surface tension
Fibrotic contraction of lung parenchyma, increasing expiratory airway compression
Fixed obstruction of the trachea, flattening only the expiratory limb

questions.explanation_html: Emphysema destroys alveolar septa and elastic tissue. Loss of recoil reduces the driving pressure for expiration, and loss of radial traction permits small noncartilaginous airways to collapse as pleural pressure becomes positive during forced expiration. This produces airflow limitation and a concave, or scooped, expiratory limb.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Alveolar-capillary thickening is characteristic of interstitial disease and does not explain hyperinflation with a low FEV1/FVC ratio.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Surfactant lowers surface tension; increased surfactant would not produce emphysematous airway collapse.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Fibrosis increases elastic recoil and tends to produce a restrictive pattern with reduced lung volumes.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: A fixed large-airway obstruction flattens both inspiratory and expiratory limbs.

questions.educational_objective: Emphysema causes expiratory flow limitation through loss of elastic recoil and radial airway traction, producing dynamic small-airway collapse and a concave expiratory flow-volume loop.

media.alt_text: Flow-volume loops comparing a normal loop with an obstructive loop that has reduced peak flow and a concave expiratory limb.
